questions.section: SECTION III: STRUCTURE QUESTIONS (40 MARKS)
questions.question:
CALCULUS
1. Show that the function f(x) = { 2x − 2 if x < 1 ; x² − 1 if x ≥ 1 } is not continuous at x = 0. [4marks]
questions.answer_guide: As printed the claim is false: near x = 0, f(x) = 2x − 2 is a polynomial, so f is continuous at x = 0 (f(0) = −2 = lim). At the join x = 1: lim(x→1⁻) = 0, lim(x→1⁺) = 0 and f(1) = 0, so f is continuous there too. The function is continuous everywhere; the question appears to contain an error. [Check against the official key.]

questions.question:
STATISTICS AND PROBABILITY
3. If P (A') = 0.6 , P (B') = 0.28, and P (A ∪ B) = 0.71 Find
  (a) P(A|B) [2marks]
  (b) P(B|A) [2marks]
questions.answer_guide:
P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.72 → P(A ∩ B) = 0.4 + 0.72 − 0.71 = 0.41
(a) P(A|B) = 0.41/0.72 ≈ 0.569
(b) P(B|A) = 0.41/0.4 = 1.025 – impossible (> 1), because P(A ∩ B) cannot exceed P(A). The data in the question are inconsistent (P(A ∪ B) must be at least 0.72). [Check against the official key.]
